set.approach: From Pincher Creek drive west on Highway 507 and follow township and range roads to a parking spot by the fence next to the natural-gas pump house beside Mill Creek. Hike south on the trails that follow Mill Creek to the Gladstone valley, cross the creek, and follow the valley trail upstream, watching for cairns where it drops into the creek bed, to Adams Lake below the wall (the camp is on the far side of the lake from where the trail arrives). From the lake walk up through the boulders and the slope above to the base of the climb.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from its anchors. The upper pitches are long, so pull the rope at the ledge below the fourth belay and use a tree there to reach the third-pitch anchor (or downclimb that short step), then continue down the lower anchors. The top-out is a loose scree slope, with a rappel anchor on the cliff above it.

review.notes: Approach from the area page and route Location; rappel descent from this route page only.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route down its own anchors.

set.approach: South of Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway side road (Highway 93A) past Athabasca Falls to Leech Lake and park at the pullout. A maintained trail leads through forest to the Lost Boys crag. The Aspen Beauty sector comes early as the trail runs beneath the cliff, just beyond the big boulder at its foot. Baby Feet starts a few metres right of Little Girly Man, at a short dark dihedral.

review.notes: Approach from Lost Boys and Aspen Beauty pages; start from route Location. No descent stated (only an anchor with rap rings).

set.approach: South of Jasper, take the Icefields Parkway side road (Highway 93A) past Athabasca Falls to Leech Lake and park at the pullout. A maintained trail leads through forest to the Lost Boys crag. Keep walking along the cliff base past the first short bolted routes to the sector where the routes become clean and tall with large rocks at their feet. The route starts just right of a low black streak and just left of a blackened boulder, working through small roofs in a faint left-facing corner before a larger roof near the top.

review.notes: Approach from Lost Boys and Aspen Beauty pages; start from the route page. Anchor is shared with another route; no descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the pullout with a garbage bin on Highway 16 between Hinton and Jasper and follow the main Cinquefoil hiking trail from the back of the lot. When the crag comes into view, take the right-hand branch at the faint fork before a rolling hill, then zigzag uphill and traverse a meadow to reach the foot of the wall. For the Cinquefoil Right sector, head right once at the wall. Fifth Gear shares its start with Starfish: clip Starfish's first bolt, then step left onto the middle bolt line.

review.notes: Approach from Cinquefoil and Cinquefoil Right pages; start from route text. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, toward Hinton. The trail starts at the far end of the pullout from the outhouse: skirt the pond, climb the steep hill, and continue up and left along the obvious trail, bearing left at forks, past a ladder to the cliffs. Crescent Wall is a small wall of bolted routes with a set of top-rope routes reached by a walk-up scramble to the right; the approach has steep sections and ladders.

review.notes: Approach from Hidden Valley, First Wall and Crescent Wall pages; the route page gives no location on the wall and no descent.

Crescent Wall is a small wall of bolted routes with a set of top-rope routes reached by a walk-up scramble to the right; the approach has steep sections and ladders. Slopers is reached by an easy scramble to its bolted anchors.

review.notes: Approach from Hidden Valley and Crescent Wall pages; route text only says easy scramble to set up a top rope, so no descent written.

set.approach: Park at the large pullout with an outhouse on Highway 16 northeast of Jasper, toward Hinton. The trail starts at the far end of the pullout from the outhouse: skirt the pond, climb the steep hill, and continue up and left along the obvious trail, bearing left at forks, past a ladder to the cliffs. First Wall is the first sector, on the left a minute or two beyond the ladder. Lower Ramp is at the far left of the wall, up the prominent gully and ramp that has a tree at its base.
set.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right of the wall, or rappel from the sport and trad anchors to the base.

review.notes: Approach from Hidden Valley and First Wall pages; start and descent from the route page, backed by the wall page noting the right-hand scramble to the top anchors.

set.approach: Park at the Goats and Glaciers lookout on the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper townsite. The wall is visible from the road. Walk from the north end of the lot into the woods and push through deadfall and underbrush, aiming slightly right of the wall toward the talus field. Climb the talus, then head left up a steep small hill and follow scree and slab, staying right of the gully, up toward the base. Distinct roofs and a broken corner system facing right are the features that identify the line.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, using the bolted stations and tree anchors. Partway down, a short walk toward climber's left along the treed ledge, past a gully and along a rock wall, leads to the next bolted station. The last rappels end at trees or the gully on climber's left, and from there a walk down scree leads to a cliff, which you follow along its base to the start of the route.

review.notes: Approach from area page and route Location; descent from the route page only (counts omitted).

set.approach: Drive the Mount Edith Cavell road, which leaves the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, to its end at the parking lot. Dune Wall is a conspicuous rock buttress at the foot of Mount Sorrow, to the right of Angel Glacier. Ford the creek and work up scree and stunted firs to the foot of the cliff. The route follows a left-facing corner reached past a ledge with a tree.

review.notes: Approach from Dune Wall page; route start from route text. No descent stated.

set.approach: Drive the Mount Edith Cavell road, which leaves the Icefields Parkway south of Jasper, to its end at the parking lot. Dune Wall is a conspicuous rock buttress at the foot of Mount Sorrow, to the right of Angel Glacier. Ford the creek and work up scree and stunted firs to the foot of the cliff. The upper corner is the biggest corner system on the wall and is easily seen from the parking lot (a second large corner just to its left is not the route). Begin on the ramp that angles up and right toward the main corner system.

review.notes: Approach from area page and route Location; rappel from the route page only (count omitted).

set.approach: Take the trail from Moraine Lake to Sentinel Pass. Grand Sentinel stands beyond the pass toward Paradise Valley and is visible to the south from the trail. Descend from the pass by the hiker's path down the right side of the valley rather than the talus on the left (the Sentinel side), which is exposed to rockfall and slides. It lies on the tower's south side.

review.notes: Approach from Sentinel Pass and Grand Sentinel pages; start from route Location; rappel mentioned on the route page only.

review.notes: Approach from Sentinel Pass and Grand Sentinel pages; route page only places it right of Cardiac. No descent stated.

set.approach: Start from the Devil's Gap trailhead in the Lake Minnewanka valley and follow the steep trail up to the base of Grey Ghost Wall, a south-facing wall.

review.notes: Approach from wall page and route Location; the Devil's Gap page only covers the road. No descent stated.

set.approach: Walk up Cougar Creek past the Cosmology crag until an island of trees sits in the creek bed. Look left for an obvious cairn and follow the trail as it winds up the hillside. The trail soon meets a first step of rock, climbed at easy fifth class, then meanders over rock, scree and dirt below a significant cliff. Descend along the cliff base for a short distance to a right-facing crack, which is the start of the first technical section. A few pieces of gear in the crack gain the ridge, with a small tree to belay from.
set.descent_text: After joining the Lady Macdonald scramble on the summit ridge, follow the hiker's scramble trail down to where Cougar Creek begins.

review.notes: Approach and descent from area and route pages (one source for the descent).

set.approach: From Jasper take Maligne Lake Road to its end at the lot with the public boat launch. The route is on the southwest face of Mount Samson, across the lake, and needs a canoe or kayak. Paddle down the eastern shore, aiming first for the tip of the large peninsula marked as Four Mile Point, then continue toward the avalanche track that comes down to the shoreline and come ashore a little north of the Samson picnic site, beneath the next big avalanche path along. Pull boats well up, since passing tour boats make wakes. On foot, gain the open avalanche slope and head for the large clump of trees on the ledge. Starting behind the single tall tree at its foot, take the ramp up and right, pull up a short loose corner of low-fifth difficulty onto a grassy shelf, and switchback up third and fourth class ground to the island of trees. Cross the broad ledge over to where the corner begins; avoid the dirty loose gully at the base of the slabs, which has loose boulders above.
set.descent_text: Do not rappel the route. From the top of the corner exit climber's left and traverse over a hill in the scree, then follow the large scree ramp down, staying off the slabs below. A rock outcrop forces a straight descent through a choke point, after which you continue the descending traverse between the slab on the left and steeper ground on the right. At the large scree run go straight down to the big avalanche track and gully. Keep to the skier's right of the gully, first through steep forest and then along the ridge beside the gully, cross the open avalanche path diagonally to the left toward the lake, then walk the shoreline back to the boats.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page and Maligne Lake page; single source for the descent (distances, times omitted).

set.approach: From Jasper take Maligne Lake Road past the north end of Medicine Lake to a small paved pullout on the right, the fourth beyond the big pullout at the lake's north end (stop before a rockslide warning sign). A rocky drainage lies a short way south of the pullout. Follow it uphill as it narrows to a creek bed, keeping left of the creek, then continue up its gravel bed until it narrows again and stay on the ridge left of the deepening gully. Climb the steep slope to treeline, exit the trees angling right back to the edge of the gully, and head for a lone small tree where the scrambling begins. Scramble the broad buttress beside the gully, then switchback across the gully on ledges or climb a crumbly fourth-class corner, to arrive on the last slope under the wall. Move rightward beneath the wall, over a wooded rise, up a large sloping ledge to the final tree on it; the line begins right beside that tree.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route; traverse back across the big ledge to reach the anchors for the first two pitches.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page (single source).

set.approach: From the Smith-Dorrien highway south of Canmore, park at the West Wind Pass trailhead and hike the good trail to the pass, from where the east face of the Rimwall is in view. Go left along the base of the wall to reach the routes. Canary in the Coal Mine takes the obvious line on the north face, past Candle in the Wind, and starts up slab.

review.notes: Approach from Rim Wall page; start and descent from route page.

set.approach: From the Smith-Dorrien highway south of Canmore, park at the West Wind Pass trailhead and hike the good trail to the pass, where the east face of the Rimwall comes into view. Cross beneath the cliff on narrow, exposed animal trails, which are well worn at first and harder to follow near the end. A red streak down the cliff, where water trickles, is an obvious landmark. The route starts well right of it, at the top of a ridge line separating two scree bowls; a piton in a small overhang where the ridge meets the wall is a place to hang a pack, and the climbing begins just left of it.
set.descent_text: From the top of the wall, a short hike with a few third-class moves leads to the summit of the Rimwall, and a good trail from there leads back to the parking area.

review.notes: Approach and descent from the route page (single source).

set.approach: From the Smith-Dorrien highway south of Canmore, park at the West Wind Pass trailhead and hike the good trail to the pass, from where the east face of the Rimwall is in view. Go left along the base of the wall to reach the routes. From the pass, hike along the base of the Rim Wall to the first obvious right-facing corner and scramble up to the base of the crack.

review.notes: Approach from Rim Wall page and route Location; no descent stated on this route page.

set.approach: From the Smith-Dorrien highway south of Canmore, park at the West Wind Pass trailhead and hike the good trail to the pass, from where the east face of the Rimwall is in view. Go left along the base of the wall to reach the routes. The Hobbit is on the left side of the wall.

review.notes: Approach from Rim Wall page and route Location; descent from the route page.

set.approach: Park at the gravel pullout near the northern edge of Jasper National Park, on the Hinton side, and follow the short gravel road toward the peak. Pass the cliff band on the left and take the trail up the northwest ridge. When the trail splits left toward the scramble route, stay with the edge of the forest on the ridge up to the steeper ground. A stretch of scrambling follows; head for the obvious left-leaning ramp and chimney feature on the northwest face. The climb starts at a two-bolt belay anchor.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the Metolius rap hangers on the route, or scramble up to the summit and follow the scramble route down.

review.notes: Approach and descent from route page (single source).

set.approach: The Ship's Prow is the large prominent feature attached to Mount Grassi above Canmore. From Canmore follow the Nordic Centre signs, then continue on Three Sisters Drive into the Homesteads area and on to Wilson Way, parking next to the boulder-edged stormwater channel. Follow the channel upstream, pass through the gap in the wooden barrier, and take the old road east, crossing the dry streambed that drains the bowl below the northwest face. Turn right onto the road along the east side of the streambed, bearing right at the fork, to a little cliff terminating a rocky spur. From there either continue east along the road to the base of the northeast ridge and climb its open east side to the prow, or drop into the west drainage, which is overgrown at first but opens to a bowl below the northwest face. Broadside is on the upper left part of the northwest face: it begins on a crack line slanting up to the right, far to the right of the pair of prominent corners and finishes in the subcorner and crack system between them.

review.notes: Approach from the Ship's Prow page; start from the route text. No descent stated.
